# ADR-005 — Published terms and simulated payment

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-03  
**Basis** [Approved US-03 Draft 2](../../spec/US-03.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-03-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 2 and 8–9

## Context

[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.

## Proposed decision

### Published terms contract

Create a Terms collection with Draft & Publish and one document per country. Use the existing country enum and a required, nonblank multiline plain-text body of at most 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Preserve the body as returned by Strapi, including paragraph breaks. Read only the published country document through the Document Service, selecting only country and body. Read up to two documents to detect duplicate publications and fail if either the country or body is invalid. Seed one fictitious, country-specific publication for Colombia and Chile in the existing startup workflow. Track seeding separately from Forms and Plans, skip countries with existing Terms documents during initial seeding, and preserve editorial changes and deliberate unpublication on subsequent starts. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid published document | `200` with the terms envelope |
| Unexpected query parameters or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| No published document | `404 TERMS_NOT_PUBLISHED` |
| Duplicate or invalid published configuration | `503 TERMS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| CMS retrieval failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse the `{ error: { code } }` envelope and `Cache-Control: no-store` on handler outcomes. Extend the same-origin, GET-only proxy allowlist and add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readTerms` to the Public role alongside Form and Plans. Generated CRUD, draft and admin access, and write credentials stay outside the public contract. The terms request carries the country in the path and no quote, consent or payment data. The proxy bypasses caching as it does for Form and Plans. [HTTP caching](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)

### Summary and consent

Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.

Read Terms on Summary entry and explicit retry through the existing `HttpClient` and signals pattern. Bind consent in memory to the active country, terms revision and the review snapshot. Compare snapshots by value using the current field identifiers, kinds and normalized values, and the selected plan ID and final money value. Navigation back to edit preserves Details and the plan candidate under their existing rules. A change to normalized quote data, plan, price or terms revision invalidates consent. Cancellation and generation checks prevent superseded responses from replacing active terms. Loading or failed terms reads leave the review available and prevent payment. [Angular HTTP requests](https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests)

### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery

1. The quote feature owns one attempt state per country. A single Pay command checks the live editable Summary prerequisites, consent and absence of a busy or completed payment. It synchronously reserves an attempt before requesting fresh country Terms. That reservation locks submission during both the refresh and the simulation. The attempt captures the country, active Summary generation, consent binding and the selected demo outcome.
2. Only the current attempt may act on the refresh result. Recheck the active country and Summary generation, current Details and plan validity, quote snapshot, and consent. A valid changed revision replaces the presented terms and clears consent. A failed or invalid read leaves a recoverable terms error. Both outcomes release the reservation without invoking the simulator. A matching revision advances directly to processing under the same reservation.
3. The local asynchronous simulator accepts only the captured Approved or Rejected outcome. Approved is the selector default. Outcome changes after reservation apply to a subsequent attempt. The simulator has no external side effects and takes no card, Details or plan data. Only the matching live attempt may settle. Rejection releases the lock with a retryable error and keeps the draft, selected plan and matching consent. A retry goes through the same Pay command and a fresh terms read. Leaving Summary, switching country or replacing the quote invalidates outstanding work. Cancel pending reads and ignore callbacks that can no longer settle. Browser Back or Forward cannot replay Pay.
4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes do not alter a settled result. History traversal and switching back to that country preserve the receipt and cannot make the same quote payable. Only an explicit start-new-quote reset under ADR-003 may clear that country's receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state. Clear the terminal lock last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Embed Terms in Form Configuration or expose generated Strapi reads | Embedding ties independent publication schedules together. Generated reads widen the public surface. The dedicated action adds one bounded response and Public permission. |
| Use `updatedAt`, `publishedAt` or an editor-entered revision | Metadata can change while the displayed text is unchanged. Manual revisions can drift from text. The content fingerprint follows what the person reviews and accepts. |
| Trust terms from Summary entry or lock only once simulation begins | Entry-only terms can miss a published change. A later lock allows overlapping Pay refreshes. Reserving before the fresh read costs one terms request per eligible Pay attempt and closes that overlap. A CMS publication after the successful read may still occur while the local simulation runs. |
| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
| Add a server-side payment endpoint | Server persistence could coordinate across tabs or devices. The approved simulator is local, so tab-scoped duplicate protection has no server or gateway dependency. |

## Verification

- Use AC-US03-01, AC-US03-02 and AC-US03-04 / T-US03-01, T-US03-02 and T-US03-04 to verify the review projection and same-country edit path in Colombia and Chile. Check that the full document is absent from the visible and accessible Summary.
- Use AC-US03-03 and AC-US03-09 / T-US03-03 and T-US03-11 to verify country-isolated published reads, revision changes and identical republishes, draft isolation, missing/invalid/unavailable terms, fresh Pay reads and consent invalidation. Verify the Public role and proxy allow only the intended content reads, and confirm a published terms edit reaches the running Angular build.
- Use AC-US03-05 through AC-US03-08 and AC-US03-10 / T-US03-05 through T-US03-09 to verify one attempt through both phases, deterministic Approved and Rejected in both countries, retry, late responses after navigation, and reload of interrupted and completed states. Check wrong-country and corrupt storage, memory fallback, and completed receipt recovery after rejected live prerequisites without opening editable Summary. T-US03-10 covers the full flow at project verification.

--- name: spec-driven-development description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when drafting a PRD or requirements document with objectives and scope, or when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea. Use when a single requirement spans several independently testable capabilities and needs decomposing into a capability map of modules before specifying. Use when evolving a shipped spec — scoping a V1, deferring ideas to a V2 backlog, or writing a follow-up spec for a change to an existing feature. --- # Spec-Driven Development ## Overview Write a structured specification before writing any code. The spec is the shared source of truth between you and the human engineer — it defines what we're building, why, and how we'll know it's done. Code without a spec is guessing. ## When to Use - Starting a new project or feature - Requirements are ambiguous or incomplete - The change touches multiple files or modules - You're about to make an architectural decision - The task would take more than 30 minutes to implement **When NOT to use:** Single-line fixes, typo corrections, or changes where requirements are unambiguous and self-contained. ## The Gated Workflow Spec-driven development has four phases, preceded by a scope check (Phase 0) that activates only when one request bundles several independently testable capabilities. Do not advance to the next phase until the current one is validated. ``` SPECIFY ──→ PLAN ──→ TASKS ──→ IMPLEMENT │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Human Human Human Human reviews reviews reviews reviews ``` ### Phase 0: Scope Check Most requests describe one capability. If this one does, skip this phase and go straight to Specify — Phase 0 exists for the exception, not the rule, and it puts no hierarchy on single-capability features. **Detection.** Decompose before specifying when a single requirement bundles several independently testable capabilities: - The requirement names distinct capabilities with their own consumers or data (e.g. identity, billing, notifications, reporting) - Acceptance criteria cluster into groups that could ship and be verified separately - One capability could be cut or replaced without rewriting the others' requirements **Propose a capability map before writing any spec.** Small and reviewable — a module table plus a build order, not a project plan: ```markdown # Capability Map: [Initiative Name] | Module id | Responsibility | Depends on | |---|---|---| | identity | Accounts, sessions, SSO | — | | billing | Plans, invoices, payments | identity | | notifications | Email and webhook fan-out | identity | | reporting | Usage dashboards | billing, notifications | Build order: identity → billing, notifications → reporting ``` - **Stable module ids.** Kebab-case, chosen once, never renamed mid-initiative. Specs, plans, and downstream commands select work by these ids instead of guessing which spec is active. - **Dependency direction, no cycles.** Arrows point one way. If two modules each need the other, they are one module. - **Interfaces live at the boundary.** The map records that `billing` depends on `identity`; the contract between them belongs in the provider module's spec (see `api-and-interface-design` for designing it). **The map is gated like every phase.** The human reviews module boundaries, dependency direction, and build order before any module spec is written. Getting the map wrong is expensive; reviewing ten lines is not. **Then recurse per module.** Run Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement for each module in dependency order. Each module gets its own spec, scoped to that module's objective, boundaries, and success criteria. Save the approved map as `spec/capability-map.md` and each module's spec alongside it in `spec/`, named by module id (`spec/SPEC-identity.md`, `spec/SPEC-billing.md`) — `/build` already accepts specs under `spec/`, and the root stays uncluttered — the map, not filename guessing, is the index of what exists. ### Phase 1: Specify Start with a high-level vision. The spec is the shared source of truth between you and the human engineer — it defines what we're building, why, and how we'll know it's done. Code without a spec is guessing. ## When to Use - Starting a new project or feature - Requirements are ambiguous or incomplete - The change touches multiple files or modules - You're about to make an architectural decision - The task would take more than 30 minutes to implement **When NOT to use:** Single-line fixes, typo corrections, or changes where requirements are unambiguous and self-contained. ## The Gated Workflow Spec-driven development has four phases, preceded by a scope check (Phase 0) that activates only when one request bundles several independently testable capabilities. Do not advance to the next phase until the current one is validated. ``` SPECIFY ──→ PLAN ──→ TASKS ──→ IMPLEMENT │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Human Human Human Human reviews reviews reviews reviews ``` ### Phase 0: Scope Check Most requests describe one capability. If this one does, skip this phase and go straight to Specify — Phase 0 exists for the exception, not the rule, and it puts no hierarchy on single-capability features. **Detection.** Decompose before specifying when a single requirement bundles several independently testable capabilities: - The requirement names distinct capabilities with their own consumers or data (e.g. identity, billing, notifications, reporting) - Acceptance criteria cluster into groups that could ship and be verified separately - One capability could be cut or replaced without rewriting the others' requirements **Propose a capability map before writing any spec.** Small and reviewable — a module table plus a build order, not a project plan: ```markdown # Capability Map: [Initiative Name] | Module id | Responsibility | Depends on | |---|---|---| | identity | Accounts, sessions, SSO | — | | billing | Plans, invoices, payments | identity | | notifications | Email and webhook fan-out | identity | | reporting | Usage dashboards | billing, notifications | Build order: identity → billing, notifications → reporting ``` - **Stable module ids.** Kebab-case, chosen once, never renamed mid-initiative. Specs, plans, and downstream commands select work by these ids instead of guessing which spec is active. - **Dependency direction, no cycles.** Arrows point one way. If two modules each need the other, they are one module. - **Interfaces live at the boundary.** The map records that `billing` depends on `identity`; the contract between them belongs in the provider module's spec (see `api-and-interface-design` for designing it). **The map is gated like every phase.** The human reviews module boundaries, dependency direction, and build order before any module spec is written. Getting the map wrong is expensive; reviewing ten lines is not. **Then recurse per module.** Run Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement for each module in dependency order. Each module gets its own spec, scoped to that module's objective, boundaries, and success criteria. Save the approved map as `spec/capability-map.md` and each module's spec alongside it in `spec/`, named by module id (`spec/SPEC-identity.md`, `spec/SPEC-billing.md`) — `/build` already accepts specs under `spec/`, and the root stays uncluttered — the map, not filename guessing, is the index of what exists. ### Phase 1: Specify Start with a high-level vision. # US-03 — Summary and simulated payment design

**Status** Proposed · Pending human design approval

**Basis** [Approved US-03](../../spec/US-03.md), [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md) and [US-02 plan selection](US-02-plan-selection.md).

## Wireframes

| View | Review frames |
| --- | --- |
| Editable Summary | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-summary-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-summary-mobile.svg) |
| Terms and payment states | [In-place variants on the compact lane](wireframes/US-03-terms-and-payment-states.svg) |
| Confirmation, including reload | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-mobile.svg) |

Each country uses the same layouts and control order. The examples use fictitious values, local currency formatting and sample terms. The app presents the active country's published terms and current field and plan labels.

## Editable Summary

- Reuse the app header, main landmark, route-entry heading focus and informational **Datos / Plan / Resumen** stepper. A review heading identifies the step. The selected country is visible in the terms heading and the plan's currency.
- Show **Titular y vehículo** as a definition list in configured order with a nearby **Editar datos** link to same-country Details. Use the projected masked document in visible and accessible text. The **Plan elegido** card shows the current plan and final price with **Cambiar plan** linking to same-country Plans. Use the approved formatter with explicit **COP** or **CLP**. Both links preserve state under the existing Details and Plans rules.
- Put **Términos y condiciones de {país}** next in reading order. Present the plain text inline with preserved paragraph breaks. The page scrolls as the text grows. The labeled, initially unchecked native consent checkbox follows the text. Its checked state reflects consent for the current quote and revision. Show **Acepta los términos para continuar.** beside the unavailable payment action while acceptance is outstanding.
- Use a native radio group with visible legend **Resultado del pago (solo demostración)** and the options **Aprobado** and **Rechazado**. Default to **Aprobado** on initial entry. Associate **No se realizará un cobro real.** with the group as help. **Simular pago** is the single Pay action for either outcome and every payment retry. Its eligibility follows ADR-005.
- At 64 rem and above, use the established centered 58 rem composition with Details and plan side by side, followed by a reading lane for terms, consent, outcome and Pay. Below 64 rem, stack the plan after Details using the same DOM order. At compact widths, retain 16–20 px side gutters and use a full-width Pay button. Use auto-height panels, wrapping labels and unbroken-value wrapping where needed. Keep the action in normal page flow.

Reuse the existing \`app-wizard-progress\` and status-panel pattern, Tailwind canvas/paper/context/ink/line tokens, existing input and focus utilities, and the approved success, error and disabled treatments. Section titles, price emphasis and the quote number follow the approved type scale. Keep 44 px link and control targets and the 48 px primary action. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md), [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Terms and payment states

| State | Visible response and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Reading terms on entry or retry | Keep the review and price visible. In the terms region show **Cargando términos…** until usable content is ready. Consent is unavailable and Pay stays disabled. |
| Terms unavailable | For empty, invalid or failed reads, including the Pay refresh, show **No pudimos cargar los términos.** with **Reintentar carga** in the terms region. Keep Details and plan. Pay stays blocked. If a successful recovery returns the same terms revision, text and quote snapshot, previously accepted consent can remain checked. Recovery returns to the review without starting payment. |
| Checking terms on Pay | Keep the review visible and reserve the single Pay action. Show **Comprobando los términos…** and disable repeat activation. The simulator begins only after the fresh read confirms the accepted terms and quote. |
| Terms changed on Pay | Replace the terms with the new text, clear consent, and show **Los términos cambiaron. Léelos y acéptalos para continuar.** before the updated text. A new acceptance followed by another **Simular pago** is required. |
| Processing | Keep the review, plan, terms and consent visible. Show **Procesando el pago simulado…** and keep Pay locked until settlement. An interrupted reload returns to the editable review if its prerequisites pass. Fresh consent is required before retry. |
| Rejected | Show **Pago simulado rechazado.** by the payment controls with **Tu cotización se conservó. Elige un resultado y vuelve a simular el pago.** The chosen **Rechazado** option remains visible. The user can select **Aprobado** or retry the chosen outcome using the same action. Retain Details, plan and still-current consent. |
| Approved | Replace all editable content with a terminal receipt. Show **Pago simulado aprobado**, **No se realizó un cobro.**, the country and a selectable **Número de cotización**. Keep the existing product header and completed stepper. On reload or return to the same completed quote, show the same reference even if published content changed. |
| Details or plan prerequisite missing | Reuse the existing redirect and recovery patterns for the earliest incomplete same-country step. Editable Summary is available after successful revalidation. |

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Use contextual anchor text for edits, an associated native checkbox label, and a native \`fieldset\` and \`legend\` for the radios. Keyboard order follows the review, terms, checkbox, radio group and Pay. Use standard Tab, Space, Enter and arrow-key behavior. Keep the disabled reason or status visible beside Pay. Preserve visible focus and the native outline in forced colors. [WAI grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
- Announce loading, fresh checks and processing through a stable polite status region. Announce actionable failures once, using the existing accessible feedback pattern. Keep focus where it is while async work runs, with the focused Pay control retained as a target during the busy state. Convey the disabled state programmatically and suppress both keyboard and pointer activation while it remains focusable. If changed terms interrupt an active Pay interaction, move focus to the updated terms heading so it precedes the new text and checkbox. On terms failure, use the recovery control as the focus destination if the initiating target disappeared or became unavailable. A failed recovery with a stable Retry control keeps focus there. A successful recovery that removes the Retry control returns focus to the terms heading. A user who moved to an edit link while waiting keeps their focus.
- On rejection, announce the result while keeping focus in place if its target is still present. The user can reach the outcome choices from Pay with Shift+Tab. On first confirmation or a restored receipt, focus its heading and expose the reference as nearby selectable text. The heading and receipt content communicate success without relying on icon or color. Use a static busy cue under reduced motion. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design verification map

| Approved criteria | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01, 02, 04 and 08 | Check both country projections, masked visible and spoken document values, option labels, currency, edit links and prerequisite recovery. |
| AC-US03-03 and 09 | Check long published terms at narrow widths, missing/invalid content, fresh Pay checks, a changed revision with renewed acceptance, and terms retry with focus and draft retention. |
| AC-US03-05, 06 and 07 | Exercise both outcome choices in each country, locked activation through both busy phases, rejection-to-approval retry, interrupted reload and same-number terminal receipt restoration. |
| AC-US03-10 | Check keyboard order, visible and unobscured focus, announcements, target sizes, reduced motion, forced colors and reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. |

The wireframes and interaction guidance are pending human design approval.
EOF`}))

BLUE, LINK, CONTROL, DIVIDER, ERROR, ERROR_TINT = '#2E6DF6', '#1748AF', '#586D91', '#CCD8EE', '#9E2F26', '#FFF2EF'
SUCCESS, SUCCESS_TINT, DISABLED = '#1F5B39', '#E8F5EC', '#E0E7F4'


class Frame:
    def __init__(self, width, height, title, desc):
        self.w, self.h = width, height
        self.parts = [
            f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc" xml:lang="en">',
            f'<title id="title">{escape(title)}</title>',
            f'<desc id="desc">{escape(desc)}</desc>',
        ]
        self.rect(0, 0, width, height, CANVAS)

    def rect(self, x, y, w, h, fill, radius=0, stroke='none'):
        self.parts.append(f'<rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="{radius}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{stroke}"/>')

    def circle(self, x, y, r, fill, stroke='none'):
        self.parts.append(f'<circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="{r}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{stroke}"/>')

    def path(self, d, stroke, width=1.5):
        self.parts.append(f'<path d="{d}" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{width}" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>')

    def rule(self, x, y, w):
        self.path(f'M{x} {y}h{w}', DIVIDER, 1)

    def text(self, x, y, message, size=16, color=INK, weight=400, anchor='start', heading=False, link=False):
        family = 'Georgia, serif' if heading else 'Arial, sans-serif'
        decoration = ' text-decoration="underline"' if link else ''
        self.parts.append(f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}" fill="{color}" font-family="{family}" font-size="{size}" font-weight="{weight}" text-anchor="{anchor}"{decoration}>{escape(message)}</text>')

    def lines(self, x, y, lines, size=16, color=SECONDARY, step=24):
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            self.text(x, y + i * step, line, size, color)

    def shell(self, done=False):
        self.parts.append('<g xml:lang="es">')
        compact = self.w < 500
        header = 64 if compact else 76
        start = 20 if compact else 58
        self.rect(0, 0, self.w, header, PAPER)
        self.rule(0, header, self.w)
        top = 19 if compact else 25
        self.path(f'M{start + 11} {top}l10 4v7q0 9-10 14q-10-5-10-14v-7Z', LINK, 1.8)
        self.path(f'M{start + 6} {top + 12}l4 4l7-8', LINK, 1.8)
        self.text(start + 32, top + 21, 'Seguro de auto', 19, INK, 700)
        center = header + 29
        points = [73, 178, 275] if compact else [425, 555, 679]
        for i, (px, label) in enumerate(zip(points, ('Datos', 'Plan', 'Resumen'))):
            current = i == 2 and not done
            self.circle(px, center, 11, BLUE if current else LINK)
            if current:
                self.text(px, center + 4, '3', 12, PAPER, 700, 'middle')
            else:
                self.path(f'M{px - 4} {center}l3 3l5-6', PAPER, 1.8)
            self.text(px + 18, center + 5, label, 14, INK if current else MUTED, 700 if current else 400)
        self.rule(20 if compact else 136, header + 58, self.w - (40 if compact else 272))

    def button(self, x, y, w, message='Simular pago', mode='primary', h=48):
        color, fg, border = {'primary': (BLUE, PAPER, 'none'), 'disabled': (DISABLED, MUTED, 'none'), 'secondary': (PAPER, LINK, CONTROL)}[mode]
        self.rect(x, y, w, h, color, 6, border)
        self.text(x + w / 2, y + h / 2 + 5, message, 15, fg, 700, 'middle')

        self.rect(x, y, 18, 18, LINK if checked else PAPER, 3, LINK if checked else CONTROL)
        if checked:

        self.text(x + 30, y + 15, 'Acepto los términos y condiciones', 15)

    def radio(self, x, y, message, checked):
        self.circle(x + 9, y, 9, PAPER, LINK if checked else CONTROL)
        if checked:

        self.text(x + 28, y + 5, message, 15, INK, 700)

        self.text(x + 20, y + 69, 'Esencial', 28, INK, heading=True)

        top = y + (78 if checked else 111)
        self.button(x, top, width, mode='primary' if checked else 'disabled')

# US-03 — Summary and simulated payment design

**Status** Proposed · Pending human design approval

**Basis** [Approved US-03](../../spec/US-03.md), [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md) and [US-02 plan selection](US-02-plan-selection.md).

## Wireframes

| View | Review frames |
| --- | --- |
| Editable Summary | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-summary-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-summary-mobile.svg) |
| Terms and payment states | [In-place variants on the compact lane](wireframes/US-03-terms-and-payment-states.svg) |
| Confirmation, including reload | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-mobile.svg) |

Each country uses the same layouts and control order. The examples use fictitious values, local currency formatting and sample terms. The app presents the active country's published terms and current field and plan labels.

## Editable Summary

- Reuse the app header, main landmark, route-entry heading focus and informational **Datos / Plan / Resumen** stepper. A review heading identifies the step. The selected country is visible in the terms heading and the plan's currency.
- Show **Titular y vehículo** as a definition list in configured order with a nearby **Editar datos** link to same-country Details. Use the projected masked document in visible and accessible text. The **Plan elegido** card shows the current plan and final price with **Cambiar plan** linking to same-country Plans. Use the approved formatter with explicit **COP** or **CLP**. Both links preserve state under the existing Details and Plans rules.
- Put **Términos y condiciones de {país}** next in reading order. Present the plain text inline with preserved paragraph breaks. The page scrolls as the text grows. The labeled, initially unchecked native consent checkbox follows the text. Its checked state reflects consent for the current quote and revision. Show **Acepta los términos para continuar.** beside the unavailable payment action while acceptance is outstanding.
- Use a native radio group with visible legend **Resultado del pago (solo demostración)** and the options **Aprobado** and **Rechazado**. Default to **Aprobado** on initial entry. Associate **No se realizará un cobro real.** with the group as help. **Simular pago** is the single Pay action for either outcome and every payment retry. Its eligibility follows ADR-005.
- At 64 rem and above, use the established centered 58 rem composition with Details and plan side by side, followed by a reading lane for terms, consent, outcome and Pay. Below 64 rem, stack the plan after Details using the same DOM order. At compact widths, retain 16–20 px side gutters and use a full-width Pay button. Use auto-height panels, wrapping labels and unbroken-value wrapping where needed. Keep the action in normal page flow.

Reuse the existing `app-wizard-progress` and status-panel pattern, Tailwind canvas/paper/context/ink/line tokens, existing input and focus utilities, and the approved success, error and disabled treatments. Section titles, price emphasis and the quote number follow the approved type scale. Keep 44 px link and control targets and the 48 px primary action. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md), [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Terms and payment states

| State | Visible response and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Reading terms on entry or retry | Keep the review and price visible. In the terms region show **Cargando términos…** until usable content is ready. Consent is unavailable and Pay stays disabled. |
| Terms unavailable | For empty, invalid or failed reads, including the Pay refresh, show **No pudimos cargar los términos.** with **Reintentar carga** in the terms region. Keep Details and plan. Pay stays blocked. If a successful recovery returns the same terms revision, text and quote snapshot, previously accepted consent can remain checked. Recovery returns to the review without starting payment. |
| Checking terms on Pay | Keep the review visible and reserve the single Pay action. Show **Comprobando los términos…** and disable repeat activation. The simulator begins only after the fresh read confirms the accepted terms and quote. |
| Terms changed on Pay | Replace the terms with the new text, clear consent, and show **Los términos cambiaron. Léelos y acéptalos para continuar.** before the updated text. A new acceptance followed by another **Simular pago** is required. |
| Processing | Keep the review, plan, terms and consent visible. Show **Procesando el pago simulado…** and keep Pay locked until settlement. An interrupted reload returns to the editable review if its prerequisites pass. Fresh consent is required before retry. |
| Rejected | Show **Pago simulado rechazado.** by the payment controls with **Tu cotización se conservó. Elige un resultado y vuelve a simular el pago.** The chosen **Rechazado** option remains visible. The user can select **Aprobado** or retry the chosen outcome using the same action. Retain Details, plan and still-current consent. |
| Approved | Replace all editable content with a terminal receipt. Show **Pago simulado aprobado**, **No se realizó un cobro.**, the country and a selectable **Número de cotización**. Keep the existing product header and completed stepper. On reload or return to the same completed quote, show the same reference even if published content changed. |
| Details or plan prerequisite missing | Reuse the existing redirect and recovery patterns for the earliest incomplete same-country step. Editable Summary is available after successful revalidation. |

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Use contextual anchor text for edits, an associated native checkbox label, and a native `fieldset` and `legend` for the radios. Keyboard order follows the review, terms, checkbox, radio group and Pay. Use standard Tab, Space, Enter and arrow-key behavior. Keep the disabled reason or status visible beside Pay. Preserve visible focus and the native outline in forced colors. [WAI grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
- Announce loading, fresh checks and processing through a stable polite status region. Announce actionable failures once, using the existing accessible feedback pattern. Keep focus where it is while async work runs, with the focused Pay control retained as a target during the busy state. Convey the disabled state programmatically and suppress both keyboard and pointer activation while it remains focusable. If changed terms interrupt an active Pay interaction, move focus to the updated terms heading so it precedes the new text and checkbox. On terms failure, use the recovery control as the focus destination if the initiating target disappeared or became unavailable. A failed recovery with a stable Retry control keeps focus there. A successful recovery that removes the Retry control returns focus to the terms heading. A user who moved to an edit link while waiting keeps their focus.
- On rejection, announce the result while keeping focus in place if its target is still present. The user can reach the outcome choices from Pay with Shift+Tab. On first confirmation or a restored receipt, focus its heading and expose the reference as nearby selectable text. The heading and receipt content communicate success without relying on icon or color. Use a static busy cue under reduced motion. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design verification map

| Approved criteria | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01, 02, 04 and 08 | Check both country projections, masked visible and spoken document values, option labels, currency, edit links and prerequisite recovery. |
| AC-US03-03 and 09 | Check long published terms at narrow widths, missing/invalid content, fresh Pay checks, a changed revision with renewed acceptance, and terms retry with focus and draft retention. |
| AC-US03-05, 06 and 07 | Exercise both outcome choices in each country, locked activation through both busy phases, rejection-to-approval retry, interrupted reload and same-number terminal receipt restoration. |
| AC-US03-10 | Check keyboard order, visible and unobscured focus, announcements, target sizes, reduced motion, forced colors and reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. |

The wireframes and interaction guidance are pending human design approval.

# US-03 — Terminal quote and restart proposal

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../docs/approvals/US-03-terminal-quote-spec-approval.md))

**Basis** [US-03 Draft 2](US-03.md), [ADR-005](../docs/adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [approved design](../docs/design/US-03-summary-and-payment.md), and the project owner's follow-up request.

## Changes to approved decisions

| Approved decision | Proposed revision |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-07 and ADR-005 restore a terminal receipt on Summary. The other wizard routes currently remain reachable through history or direct navigation. | Make confirmation the only reachable wizard step for an approved quote until the user explicitly starts a new quote. |
| ADR-005 persists only the country and quote number. The approved confirmation shows the reference. | Preserve a frozen, masked review of the completed Details, chosen plan and final price with the receipt. Restore the same review after reload even if Strapi content changes. This requires revising the minimal receipt storage decision. |
| ADR-005 defines a future reset boundary. The approved design has no reset action. | Add one **Iniciar una nueva cotización** action on the confirmation screen and return to the current country's Details after reset. |

## Proposed acceptance criteria and regression coverage

| ID | Behavior | Regression verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-US03-R01 | After approval, opening the same country's Details or Plans URL or reaching either via Back or Forward redirects to confirmation without exposing editable fields or plan controls. The receipt and protection survive reload. The other country's wizard remains independent. | In CO and CL, approve a quote, exercise direct entry and browser history, and reload. Verify the same reference, no editable controls and country isolation. |
| AC-US03-R02 | Confirmation displays the approval, quote reference and read-only Details and plan/final price as captured at approval. The document remains masked. Changes to live form labels, plan prices or availability do not alter a completed quote. | In both countries, verify the approved projection and masked value, then reload after a changed or unavailable catalog and compare the receipt and projection. |
| AC-US03-R03 | Starting a new quote clears the current country's entered data, selected plan, consent, payment attempt and terminal receipt from memory and wizard persistence. It opens same-country Details with configured defaults. Subsequent reloads and old history entries cannot restore the previous approval. | In both countries, reset after approval, reload and revisit the old Summary URL. Verify the old reference and selection are absent, new Details can be entered, and a subsequent approval has a new reference. |

## Decisions for architecture and design review

- Propose persisting only the frozen display projection needed for the receipt, including the already masked document value. Keep the existing country- and tab-scoped boundary. Do not derive historical values from mutable drafts or live content after approval.

Display the full read-only review on newly approved receipts. Do not reconstruct an older completed quote from mutable data.

- Extend the existing confirmation design with a read-only review and a keyboard-accessible restart action that moves focus to the same-country Details heading after success.

# ADR-005 amendment — Terminal quote and restart

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-03-terminal-quote-architecture-approval.md))

**Applies to** US-03, AC-US03-R01 through AC-US03-R04

**Basis** [Approved terminal quote revision](../../spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md), [revision approval](../approvals/US-03-terminal-quote-spec-approval.md) and [ADR-005](ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md)

## Context

The approved revision changes the completed quote behavior in steps 4 and 5 of ADR-005. The existing Angular wizard reads a minimal receipt on Summary, but can still open editable Details and Plans with that receipt present. It stores editable Details, the plan candidate and the receipt in independent country-scoped keys. The revision makes confirmation terminal across wizard routes, restores the captured review and introduces an explicit country-scoped restart. The content and payment boundaries in [ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) and ADR-005 continue to apply to unfinished quotes.

## Proposed decisions

### Gate the wizard on the terminal receipt

Keep `/:country/quote/summary` as the confirmation route for a completed quote. Continue using the existing route parameter subscription, including for a reused quote component and browser history. Decode the country and synchronously resolve its terminal receipt before exposing any editable route state or requesting live quote content. A valid receipt takes precedence over Details, Plans and editable Summary. Replace an attempted same-country Details or Plans history entry with the canonical Summary URL and render only confirmation. No editable control is instantiated while the redirect is pending. Confirmation reads the receipt directly and has no form, catalog or terms prerequisite. Keep the terminal check reactive so successful completion also switches the current Summary to confirmation without waiting for a navigation. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state) · [Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)

Reuse the route and attempt generations to suppress superseded work at navigation and restart. A retained event or delayed response must not re-enter an editable step, persist an old draft or plan, or settle an attempt after the quote becomes terminal or its state is reset. Receipt lookup and redirect decisions always use the canonical active country. Rejection creates no receipt and keeps the existing edit, plan selection and retry behavior, including a fresh terms check on Pay.

### Freeze the review at approval

After the live attempt passes its final eligibility check, use the existing review projector to capture ordered label and display-value rows, including the already masked identity document. Capture the chosen plan's displayed name and validated final `{ amountMinor, currency }` at the same transition. Generate the existing opaque quote reference once and commit the immutable receipt as one snapshot. Copy display values out of the editable state. Restore and display the snapshot with the existing country money formatter. A published change, removal or outage cannot alter it. Treat values as plain text in both visible and accessible output.

Store `{ version: 2, country, number, review: { rows, planName, price } }` in the existing per-country receipt key, `quote-receipt-v1:<country>`. The key stays stable. The envelope version determines the decoder. Persist only row id, display label and display value for each row, alongside the plan name and typed price. Keep the raw document, full draft, full plan catalog, terms, consent and attempt data out of the receipt.

Validate one bounded envelope before rendering. Check version, country, quote reference format, ordered rows with unique valid field ids, text limits and country money. Use the existing form and plan contract limits as the source for bounds. The current contract permits 40 rows, field ids of up to 40 safe characters, labels and plan names of up to 240 UTF-16 code units, and free text of up to 256 Unicode code points. A projected value therefore needs up to 512 UTF-16 code units, including supplementary characters. The field and string limits plus worst-case JSON escaping, price and envelope fit within a 200,000 UTF-16 code unit pre-parse limit. Use only the decoded fields for rendering. An invalid version 2 record does not fall back to a reference-only receipt. If writing a valid receipt fails, preserve the full terminal receipt and duplicate lock in memory under ADR-003 and surface that reload recovery is unavailable. Never write a partial or version 1 substitute.

Continue decoding the existing version 1 envelope in that same key with its original bounds and country and number checks. It restores the original reference, terminal gate and restart behavior. Its historical review is unavailable. There is no backfill from mutable state and no migration write during restore. The single key avoids a second legacy lookup that could revive an old receipt after restart.

### Restart and release the terminal lock last

Use one restart command for the active country and terminal receipt. Run the synchronous persistence sequence through the existing state owners, with an explicit outcome for every storage action. The current draft and candidate persistence helpers can swallow failures for ordinary edits. Restart must observe failures and may not use silent success from those paths. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

1. Keep confirmation and the terminal guard in place throughout reset. Invalidate pending country-scoped form, plan, terms and payment work before clearing persisted state. Ignore repeated reset requests while a reset is in progress.
2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.

If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Gate only Summary or restore by replaying live reads | An editable route could reopen the flow, and historical values could change with publication or retrieval failures. The route gate and stored review remove both dependencies. |
| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |

## Verification

- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R02** — In each country, compare the masked captured review, amount and reference after changed or unavailable Strapi content. Test the worst-case valid projection against the codec, and reject corrupted and wrong-country envelopes. Verify that failed writes retain the full review in memory.
- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R04** — In both countries, verify rejection retains the draft and plan candidate, allows edit routes, and retries using the existing consent and fresh-terms rules.

[HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

1. Keep confirmation and the terminal guard in place throughout reset. Invalidate pending country-scoped form, plan, terms and payment work before clearing persisted state. Ignore repeated reset requests while a reset is in progress.
2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.

If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Gate only Summary or restore by replaying live reads | An editable route could reopen the flow, and historical values could change with publication or retrieval failures. The route gate and stored review remove both dependencies. |
| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |

## Verification

- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R02** — In each country, compare the masked captured review, amount and reference after changed or unavailable Strapi content. Test the worst-case valid projection against the codec, and reject corrupted and wrong-country envelopes. Verify that failed writes retain the full review in memory.
- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R04** — In both countries, verify rejection retains the draft and plan candidate, allows edit routes, and retries using the existing consent and fresh-terms rules.

# US-03 — Summary and simulated payment design

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-03-design-approval.md))

**Basis** [Approved US-03](../../spec/US-03.md), [ADR-005](../adr/ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md), [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md) and [US-02 plan selection](US-02-plan-selection.md).

## Wireframes

| View | Review frames |
| --- | --- |
| Editable Summary | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-summary-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-summary-mobile.svg) |
| Terms and payment states | [In-place variants on the compact lane](wireframes/US-03-terms-and-payment-states.svg) |
| Confirmation, including reload | [Desktop · Colombia](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-desktop.svg) · [Mobile · Chile](wireframes/US-03-confirmation-mobile.svg) |

Each country uses the same layouts and control order. The initial country selection supplies the context for the quote. Keep country names out of app-authored Summary, terms headings, payment states, confirmation and accessibility copy. Use the active country's approved currency formatting and show Strapi content as published or configured, including terms, plan names and form labels. The frames use fictitious quote values and short illustrative terms excerpts.

## Editable Summary

- Reuse the app header, main landmark, route-entry heading focus and informational **Datos / Plan / Resumen** stepper. A review heading identifies the step. The plan's currency follows the active country.
- Show **Titular y vehículo** in a white bordered card at every width, with a definition list in configured order and a nearby **Editar datos** link to same-country Details. Use the projected masked document in visible and accessible text. The **Plan elegido** card shows the current plan and final price with **Cambiar plan** linking to same-country Plans. Use the approved formatter with explicit **COP** or **CLP**. Both links preserve state under the existing Details and Plans rules. The wireframes show a shorter example field list. Show every configured, entered value in the review, including accessories when configured and entered.
- Put **Términos y condiciones** next in reading order. Present the plain text inline with preserved paragraph breaks. The page scrolls as the text grows. The labeled, initially unchecked native consent checkbox follows the text. Its checked state reflects consent for the current quote and revision. Show **Acepta los términos para continuar.** beside the unavailable payment action while acceptance is outstanding.
- Use a native radio group with visible legend **Resultado del pago (solo demostración)** and the options **Aprobado** and **Rechazado**. Default to **Aprobado** on initial entry. Associate **No se realizará un cobro real.** with the group as help. **Simular pago** is the single Pay action for either outcome and every payment retry. Its eligibility follows ADR-005.
- At 64 rem and above, use the established centered 58 rem composition. Place the Details panel on the left and stack the selected plan, terms, consent, outcome and Pay in the right column. Align the Details panel with the price card at the top. Below 64 rem, stack the same content in one column using the same DOM order. At compact widths, retain 16–20 px side gutters and use a full-width Pay button. Use auto-height panels, wrapping labels and unbroken-value wrapping where needed. Keep the action in normal page flow.

Reuse the existing `app-wizard-progress` and status-panel pattern, Tailwind canvas/paper/context/ink/line tokens, existing input and focus utilities, and the approved success, error and disabled treatments. Section titles, price emphasis and the quote number follow the approved type scale. Keep 44 px link and control targets and the 48 px primary action. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md), [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Terms and payment states

| State | Visible response and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Reading terms on entry or retry | Keep the review and price visible. In the terms region show **Cargando términos…** until usable content is ready. Consent is unavailable and Pay stays disabled. |
| Terms unavailable | For empty, invalid or failed reads, including the Pay refresh, show **No pudimos cargar los términos.** with **Reintentar carga** in the terms region. Keep Details and plan. Pay stays blocked. If a successful recovery returns the same terms revision, text and quote snapshot, previously accepted consent can remain checked. Recovery returns to the review without starting payment. |
| Checking terms on Pay | Keep the review visible and reserve the single Pay action. Show **Comprobando los términos…** and disable repeat activation. The simulator begins only after the fresh read confirms the accepted terms and quote. |
| Terms changed on Pay | Replace the terms with the new text, clear consent, and show **Los términos cambiaron. Léelos y acéptalos para continuar.** before the updated text. A new acceptance followed by another **Simular pago** is required. |
| Processing | Keep the review, plan, terms and consent visible. Show **Procesando el pago simulado…** and keep Pay locked until settlement. An interrupted reload returns to the editable review if its prerequisites pass. Fresh consent is required before retry. |
| Rejected | Show **Pago simulado rechazado.** by the payment controls with **Tu cotización se conservó. Elige un resultado y vuelve a simular el pago.** The chosen **Rechazado** option remains visible. The user can select **Aprobado** or retry the chosen outcome using the same action. Retain Details, plan and still-current consent. |
| Approved | Replace all editable content with a terminal receipt. Center the checkmark, **Pago simulado aprobado** heading and selectable **Número de cotización** in the receipt. Use an opaque reference without a country prefix. Keep the existing product header and completed stepper. On reload or return to the same completed quote, show the same reference even if published content changed. |
| Details or plan prerequisite missing | Reuse the existing redirect and recovery patterns for the earliest incomplete same-country step. Editable Summary is available after successful revalidation. |

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Use contextual anchor text for edits, an associated native checkbox label, and a native `fieldset` and `legend` for the radios. Keyboard order follows the review, terms, checkbox, radio group and Pay. Use standard Tab, Space, Enter and arrow-key behavior. Keep the disabled reason or status visible beside Pay. Preserve visible focus and the native outline in forced colors. [WAI grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
- Announce loading, fresh checks and processing through a stable polite status region. Announce actionable failures once, using the existing accessible feedback pattern. Keep focus where it is while async work runs, with the focused Pay control retained as a target during the busy state. Convey the disabled state programmatically and suppress both keyboard and pointer activation while it remains focusable. If changed terms interrupt an active Pay interaction, move focus to the updated terms heading so it precedes the new text and checkbox. On terms failure, use the recovery control as the focus destination if the initiating target disappeared or became unavailable. A failed recovery with a stable Retry control keeps focus there. A successful recovery that removes the Retry control returns focus to the terms heading. A user who moved to an edit link while waiting keeps their focus.
- On rejection, announce the result while keeping focus in place if its target is still present. The user can reach the outcome choices from Pay with Shift+Tab. On first confirmation or a restored receipt, focus its heading and expose the reference as nearby selectable text. The heading and receipt content communicate success without relying on icon or color. Use a static busy cue under reduced motion. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design verification map

| Approved criteria | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-01, 02, 04 and 08 | Check both country projections, masked visible and spoken document values, option labels, currency, country-neutral app copy, edit links and prerequisite recovery. |
| AC-US03-03 and 09 | Check long published terms at narrow widths, missing/invalid content, fresh Pay checks, a changed revision with renewed acceptance, and terms retry with focus and draft retention. |
| AC-US03-05, 06 and 07 | Exercise both outcome choices in each country, locked activation through both busy phases, rejection-to-approval retry, interrupted reload and same-number terminal receipt restoration. |
| AC-US03-10 | Check keyboard order, visible and unobscured focus, announcements, target sizes, reduced motion, forced colors and reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom. |

The project owner approved the wireframes and interaction guidance.

# US-03 — Terminal quote and restart design

**Status** Proposed · Pending human design approval

**Basis** [Approved terminal quote revision](../../spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md), [approved ADR-005 amendment](../adr/ADR-005-amendment-terminal-quote.md), [US-03 design](US-03-summary-and-payment.md) and [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md).

| View | Wireframe |
| --- | --- |
| Completed quote with captured review | [Desktop](wireframes/US-03-terminal-quote-desktop.svg) · [Mobile](wireframes/US-03-terminal-quote-mobile.svg) |
| Receipt and restart notices | [Legacy receipt, reload warning and retry excerpts](wireframes/US-03-terminal-quote-notices.svg) |

## Confirmation

- Preserve the completed stepper and centered checkmark, **Pago aprobado** heading and selectable **Número de cotización**. Use the opaque receipt reference as displayed at approval. The caption, heading, reference, captured review and restart action follow the same reading order at every width.
- Place the captured **Titular y vehículo** definition list and **Plan elegido** card below the receipt header. Use the captured display labels and values in their original order, including the masked document value, and show the captured plan name and **Precio final** using the existing locale currency formatter. Treat every captured value as plain text. The receipt has only read-only content and one quote restart action. Use country-neutral app copy.
- Reuse the existing paper, border and context colors. At 64 rem and above, place the review beside the plan in the centered 58 rem wizard lane. At narrower widths stack the same panels in reading order with the existing side gutters. Use the bordered paper card for the review and allow long labels, document values, prices and references to wrap. Size the cards to their contents and keep the restart control in page flow. Use a full-width 48 px minimum restart button on compact screens, and a centered content-width button on wide screens. [US-01 design system](US-01-design-system.md)
- Put **Iniciar una nueva cotización** after the receipt content. Activation starts the same-country reset. Keep the receipt and its focusable restart control in place while the reset is in progress, with activation suppressed until it settles. After a successful reset, land on the current country's Details with configured defaults, and focus **Datos para cotizar**. Subsequent visits to old routes follow unfinished-quote prerequisites. Use the existing Details recovery if its configuration fails to load after the reset.

## Route and recovery behavior

| State | Design response |
| --- | --- |
| Approval, reload, direct entry or browser history | Render the same terminal confirmation for the completed quote. The same country's Details or Plans route resolves to canonical Summary before showing any editable UI. Focus **Pago aprobado** when confirmation becomes the visible screen, including from direct and history navigation. Keep the completed stepper informational. The other country's wizard follows its own state. |
| Legacy receipt with unavailable review | Keep the approval, original reference and restart action. In place of the captured review, show **El detalle de esta cotización no está disponible.** Omit the review and plan cards. Apply the same route protection and reset behavior. |
| Receipt available in memory only | Keep the complete confirmation. Below the reference, display **Si recargas la página, es posible que no puedas recuperar esta cotización.** The restart action still attempts the approved cleanup. |
| Restart fails before commit | Keep the receipt, reference and any captured review. Immediately before the existing button show **No pudimos iniciar una nueva cotización. Inténtalo de nuevo.** Announce the error once and keep focus on the restart button when it initiated the attempt. The same action is available for retry. |
| Payment rejected | Keep the existing editable Summary, **Pago rechazado.** alert and **Resultado de prueba** radio group. **Editar datos** and **Cambiar plan** continue to open the corresponding steps. **Pagar** retries with the chosen outcome and the fresh terms check. The quote draft and eligible plan candidate follow the existing rules. |

## Accessibility and verification

Use the existing main landmark and skip link. Use a single confirmation heading as the programmatic focus target and read the quote number as a labeled selectable value. The checkmark is decorative. Preserve the native button semantics, the shared visible focus treatment including forced colors, and normal document scroll. Use a stable polite status for a visible pending reset message if needed and an announced error for a failed reset. Preserve the user's focus on in-place retry and avoid announcing the heading twice when navigation takes focus. [WCAG focus order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html), [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

| Approved criterion | Checks for implementation and QA |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US03-R01 | In both countries, test Back, Forward, direct Details and Plans URLs and reload after approval. Confirm canonical Summary, a stable reference and confirmation focus, without exposure of editable controls. Check country independence and a restored legacy receipt. |
| AC-US03-R02 | Confirm the captured values, masking, labels, plan and price remain identical after content changes or outages. Test memory-only receipt messaging, 320 CSS px reflow, zoom and long content. |
| AC-US03-R03 | Activate restart by keyboard. Confirm Details focus and configured defaults on success, absence of the old receipt after reload and history navigation, and an announced, actionable failure with focus retained on retry. |
| AC-US03-R04 | After rejection, follow each edit link, return with the retained draft and eligible selection, and approve through the existing fresh terms and Pay flow. |
EOF
